applies_why: The judge text marks the Luke 2:48-49 point UNDERDETERMINED by treating 'thy father' as qualified by 'my Father's business,' which invokes the two-sense situation governed by K-S2.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed reading it as barring UNDERDETERMINED whenever one verse holds two simultaneous senses, versus reading it as barring only reliance on a single verse's silence; the judge's stated qualification uses the two-sense situation.
why: By calling the point UNDERDETERMINED after treating 'thy father' and 'my Father' as simultaneous qualified senses, the judge leaves open what K-S2 says is not open, since both senses stand.
